attempts.user_message:
Please review the following manuscript.

Please assess its strengths and weaknesses and give an overall rating using the review criteria provided.

Here is the manuscript:

/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b03/review-experiment-dqltld57/call-4490ad5e0a704e74b72d89cddd49d486/manuscript.pdf

command_activity.command: /bin/bash -c 'ls -l manuscript.pdf; command -v pdftotext; command -v pdftoppm; command -v pdfinfo; command -v python3'

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
import importlib.util
for name in ['pypdf','pdfplumber','fitz','PIL']:
 print(name, bool(importlib.util.find_spec(name)))
PY"

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
p=Path('tmp/pdfs')
p.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('Pages:',len(r.pages))
for i,page in enumerate(r.pages,1):
 t=page.extract_text(extraction_mode='layout')
 (p/f'page-{i:02d}.txt').write_text(t)
 print(f'PAGE {i}: {len(t)} chars')
(p/'manuscript.txt').write_text('\\n\\n'.join(f'PAGE {i}\\n'+(p/f'page-{i:02d}.txt').read_text() for i in range(1,len(r.pages)+1)))
print((p/'page-01.txt').read_text())
PY"

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
p=Path('tmp/pdfs')
for i in range(1,20):
 for suffix in ('txt','png'):
  (p/f'page-{i:02d}.{suffix}').unlink(missing_ok=True)
(p/'manuscript.txt').unlink(missing_ok=True)
print('Removed temporary extraction and rendering files.')
PY"

strengths: MaskSub provides a useful, technically coherent training contribution: a shared network learns from labels on unmasked inputs and from detached predictions on heavily masked inputs. The method is simple, adds no inference parameters, and integrates with established supervised recipes.

The central ImageNet results are well supported. Table 1 reports gains of 0.6–0.7 percentage points across ViT sizes after 400 epochs and 0.3–0.5 after 800 epochs. Table A.13 includes three-run statistics, with ViT-B improving from 83.46±0.04 to 84.08±0.02.

Training-budget comparisons substantiate practical value despite the additional forward/backward pass. Table 8 shows ViT-B reaching 84.1% in 25 GPU-days versus 83.7% in 26 GPU-days for longer baseline training. Table 9 also demonstrates a favorable accuracy/cost tradeoff against CoSub.

Evaluation extends substantially beyond one classification setting: ResNet and Swin training, pretrained-model fine-tuning, transfer learning, segmentation, detection, and robustness. For example, ViT-B ImageNet-A accuracy improves from 36.8 to 41.9 in Table A.4. This breadth strengthens the case for acceptance.

The appendix provides meaningful ablations and useful reproduction details. Removing KD reduces ViT-B accuracy from 84.1 to 83.6 in Table A.6; masking-ratio and loss-weight sweeps support the default configuration. Algorithm 1, detailed recipe tables, and the stated code release support reproducibility.
weaknesses: Conceptual novelty is limited relative to existing consistency training and self-distillation. With detached teacher probabilities, Equation 3's cross-entropy has the same optimization gradient as KL consistency loss because the teacher entropy is constant. Consequently, the claimed distinction from UDA based on 'distillation' versus 'consistency' is unconvincing. The main contribution is the effective supervised application and computationally efficient masking.

The proposed automatic difficulty-control mechanism is only partially established. Figure 2's aggregate gradient norms are consistent with the explanation, but do not establish the claim that masking effectively applies exclusively to successfully predicted samples. The auxiliary objective applies to every sample, and confidently incorrect predictions can also provide strong targets. This limits the mechanistic interpretation.

The plug-in benefits have meaningful exceptions. With a MaskSub-pretrained ViT-B, adding MaskSub during fine-tuning decreases CIFAR-100 accuracy from 91.89 to 89.55 (Table A.10). Section 4.2 also states that CLIP fine-tuning matches the baseline's best-epoch accuracy; its reported advantage concerns the final epoch. These findings qualify the manuscript's broad claims of consistent improvement.

Evidence is less conclusive for some auxiliary results. The 0.1-point BEiTv2 and 0.2-point detection gains lack reported uncertainty estimates, although repetitions are supplied for key ViT experiments. GLUE reproduction is also underspecified: Appendix B omits training hyperparameters and the adaptation of the distillation objective to STS-B regression. These limitations weaken the peripheral claims without overturning the stronger vision evidence.
